question: Which mechanism is at the core of the transformer architecture?
options: A recurrent hidden state
Convolutional pooling
Decision tree splitting
Self-attention
explanation: Transformers rely on self-attention to let every token draw information from every other token.

question: What is tokenization in NLP?
options: Encrypting text before sending it to a model
Splitting text into smaller units such as words or subwords
Removing all punctuation and numbers from text
Translating text into a different language
explanation: Tokenization converts raw text into discrete units that a model can map to IDs and embeddings.

question: What is a word embedding?
options: A list of all words sorted alphabetically
A dense vector representation that captures word meaning
A rule that maps words to their part of speech
A one-character code assigned to each word
explanation: Embeddings place words in a vector space where semantically similar words lie close together.

question: In text preprocessing, what are stop words?
options: Special tokens that mark the end of a generated sequence
Offensive words removed by content filters
Rare words that appear only once in a corpus
Very common words like the and is that are often filtered out
explanation: Stop words carry little topical meaning, so classic NLP pipelines often remove them.

question: What is an advantage of subword tokenization such as byte-pair encoding?
options: It guarantees every word maps to exactly one token
It handles rare and unseen words by breaking them into known pieces
It removes the need for an embedding layer
It makes sequences longer to improve accuracy
explanation: Subword vocabularies keep size manageable while still representing any word as a sequence of known units.

question: What is the benefit of multi-head attention?
options: It reduces the number of tokens in the input sequence
It allows training without any positional information
It replaces the feed-forward layers in each block
It lets the model attend to different kinds of relationships in parallel subspaces
explanation: Each head has its own projections, so different heads can specialize in different patterns such as syntax or coreference.

question: What attention masking does a decoder-only language model use during training?
options: Causal masking, so each token attends only to earlier tokens
Bidirectional attention over the full sequence
Random masking of tokens that must be reconstructed
No attention, only feed-forward layers
explanation: Causal masks stop tokens from seeing the future, matching the left-to-right next-token prediction objective.

subject: ai
question: What does self-attention compute for each token?
options: A weighted combination of all tokens' representations based on relevance
The probability that the token is a stop word
A fixed embedding independent of surrounding words
A hidden state passed strictly from left to right
explanation: Each token's query is compared to every key, and the resulting weights mix the value vectors into a context-aware representation.

subject: ai
question: Why is a BERT-style masked language model not directly suited to free-form text generation?
options: It has no embedding layer for output tokens
It can only process sentences of five words
It is trained with bidirectional context to fill masked tokens, not to predict text left to right
It uses recurrent layers that cannot generate text
explanation: Generation requires predicting the next token from past context only, which a bidirectional masked objective does not train.

question: How does the compute and memory cost of standard self-attention scale with sequence length n?
options: Quadratically in n
Logarithmically in n
Linearly in n
It stays constant in n
explanation: Every token attends to every other token, producing an n by n attention matrix.

question: Why are attention scores divided by the square root of the key dimension?
options: To keep large dot products from pushing softmax into regions with tiny gradients
To reduce the memory needed to store keys
To make attention causal for decoder models
To ensure the attention weights sum to exactly one
explanation: Dot products grow with dimension; scaling keeps their variance stable so softmax does not saturate.

question: Why do transformers need positional encodings?
options: Self-attention is permutation-invariant, so token order must be injected explicitly
To reduce the vocabulary size of the tokenizer
To stop the model from attending to padding
To make attention weights sum to one
explanation: Without position information, attention treats the input as an unordered set of tokens.
